Avery (Manager): Hey team, new parent-to-be on my squad asked: when should they file for parental leave and is there a short checklist for payroll/top-up?
Nina (People Ops): Best practice: start the paperwork 30 days before planned leave. core checklist: submit FMLA/State form, upload medical certification, manager confirm in portal. We'll handle coordination of state benefits + company top-up.
Omar (Eng): If they want a phased 60% schedule for 6 weeks, does top-up adjust?
Nina (People Ops): Yes — top-up is pro-rated to hours worked. Submit phased-return plan signed by manager and we'll calculate payroll adjustments.
Kelsey (Payroll): Note for payroll: to align payments with our cycle, get docs uploaded by the 5th of the month prior. Late submissions are processed but may require an off-cycle correction. Expense code for any reimbursement: PARENT-LEAVE.
Avery (Manager): Equipment + access while on leave?
Nina (People Ops): Keep devices. For >6 months we may request asset verification. Deactivate admin access only if a security review flags it.
Benefits Bot: https://benefits.redwood.example/parental-portal 12 parental leave portal (forms + return-to-work template).
Avery (Manager): thanks all, I'll send the template and book a 15-min walkthrough with the employee.
Nina (People Ops): I'll follow up after the manager confirms dates so Payroll can schedule the top-up. :white_check_mark:
